pr.title: Finish a review's cleanup through project review finish
pr.head: f009d62d637f9c8e4f0498e9a4a71c55349ae9e3

summary: A Projector review leaves things behind on the reviewer's machine and on GitHub. project review setup makes a scratch worktree for each head it reviews, holds a lock, writes a state file, and posts a start comment, an issue comment that tells readers a review of the pull request is in progress. project review publish deletes the start comment, but nothing removed the worktrees or the state. The skills told the agent to remove them by hand, and to delete a stopped session's start comment with gh api.

Those hand steps cause two problems. A worktree removed by hand leaves the state file naming a path that is gone. Claude Code's auto mode can also refuse a raw gh api -X DELETE as a write to an external system, so the cleanup stalls.
This pull request moves the cleanup into commands:

• project review finish <pr> ends one model's review of the pull request on this machine. It deletes that model's start comments that no longer mean a review in progress, removes every scratch worktree the state lists, clears the locks, and deletes the state. The loop's record of published reviews stays. It refuses while a review is set up and unpublished, unless you pass --force.
  • project review setup --replace <comment-id> deletes a stopped session's start comment, after it checks that the comment is this model's start comment on this pull request.
  • project init adds a permission rule, Bash(project review finish *), to Claude Code settings, and a matching rule to the Codex rules file, so auto mode does not refuse finish.
The review-pr and start-review-loop skills now name these commands instead of the hand steps, and docs/cli.md documents them.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Start comment: the issue comment setup posts, with a projector-start marker naming the head SHA and the model. It means a review is in progress.
  • Live: what is_live decides about a start comment. A comment stops being live once its model posts a verdict on its head after the comment was created, or once a day passes since its last edit.
  • State: state.json under prs/<owner>/<repo>/<pr>/<model-key>/ in the review state directory. It records the head, the checkout, the worktrees, and the start comment of one model's review.
  • Loop record: loops/<id>/published.json, the review ids a review loop published. finish keeps it.

groups.title: The finish command and setup --replace
groups.kicker: The review state code that deletes start comments and removes worktrees
intro: All the behavior lives in src/projector/review.py, the module behind every project review command. It adds finish and its helpers, a --replace path in setup, and one change to what setup writes to the state.

1. finish finds the review. It takes the repository from --repo, or else from the origin of the checkout it runs in, through named_repo, the resolver hold also uses. It never takes the repository from review state, so a run in one repository cannot end another repository's review of a pull request with the same number. It refuses when only another repository has a review of that number set up here, and when a state file names a different repository. With nothing set up, it returns early and asks GitHub nothing.
  2. It refuses an unpublished review. A state that still records a start comment belongs to a review that has not been published. Without --force, finish raises before it changes anything.
  3. It deletes start comments. finished_starts lists the reviewer's start comments for this model, and selects the review's own comment and every one that is_live says is no longer live. finish deletes each one with the reviewer's token.
  4. It removes worktrees. remove_worktrees runs git worktree remove --force in the checkout for each listed path. When Git refuses and the path is under the review's own worktree folder, it deletes the folder outright. Then it runs git worktree prune.
  5. It clears the rest. It releases the locks, and deletes review.json, the state file, and the empty folder.

For finish to remove every worktree, the state must list them all. A review loop keeps each head's worktree between heads, so setup now carries the earlier state's worktrees list forward instead of starting it fresh.

checks.text: publish sets the state's start_comment to None after it deletes the comment, so finish without --force runs after a publish that completed. I traced this in publish at the head, and the FinishTests cases that publish and then finish pass.

files.note: Adds finish, unfinished, finished_starts, remove_worktrees, finish_lines, and check_replaceable. Also carries worktrees forward in setup, and renames hold_repo to named_repo for both commands, and rewrites four refusal messages to name a command instead of a hand step.

checks.text: A review set up for another repository with the same pull request number stops finish before it deletes anything. I ran a reproduction against f009d62: from an other/repo checkout, finish 1 --force --model claude-opus-5-5 exits 1, and the acme/app#1 review's start comment, worktree, and state remain.
The list keeps the earlier heads' worktrees, with duplicates dropped, so a re-review of an unchanged head lists its worktree once. A path that no longer exists is skipped when finish runs.

--replace accepts only a start comment that the reviewer posted on this pull request for the same model. The comment is deleted after the new start comment is posted, in the same loop that deletes the comment the old state recorded.
shutil.rmtree runs only for a path under the review's own worktree folder, and only after Git refused to remove it, as it does when the checkout is gone.
A publish that posted its review and stopped before it deleted the start comment gets its own refusal, which says to run the same publish again.

groups.title: Command line and permission rules
groups.kicker: The finish subcommand, the --replace flag, and the rule init adds
intro: src/projector/cli.py registers finish with the same pr, --repo, --state-dir, --loop, --json, and --model options as the other review commands, plus --force. It adds --replace to setup.

src/projector/permissions.py holds the rules project init writes into the user's own Claude Code settings and Codex rules file. Auto mode refuses a deletion through a raw gh api call, but an allow rule for the command resolves it first. The new rule follows the one for project review hold, which exists for the same reason.

checks.text: Anyone who ran project init before this change lacks the new rule, so project review rules exits 1 for them until they run init again in a terminal.

files.note: Registers finish and setup --replace, dispatches finish before the code that the other commands share, and calls named_repo for hold.

checks.text: finish always exits 0 when it does not raise, including when it finds nothing to finish.

files.note: Adds Bash(project review finish *) to RULES and a prefix_rule for project review finish to the Codex rules.

groups.title: Skill instructions
groups.kicker: The review skills now name the commands in place of hand cleanup
intro: An agent follows these files as instructions, so a change here changes what a review does. review-pr now runs project review finish after the summary, and runs setup --replace when a stopped session's start comment blocks setup. It tells the agent never to delete a start comment through gh api. start-review-loop tells a subagent to run finish --force when its pull request closes.

files.note: Replaces three hand steps: delete a stopped session's comment, delete a leftover comment, and remove the scratch worktree. Adds finish to the commands that take --model.

checks.text: A leftover start comment, from a session that stopped between publishing and deleting, now waits for the next finish by that model on this machine. finish deletes it only when this machine has a state for the review.

files.note: The CLOSED step now runs project review finish <number> --repo <owner>/<repo> --force with --loop and --model. finish joins the commands the loop passes both flags to, and the rules check names its rule. The step keeps project loop remove, which main added for the tracked file.

checks.text: --repo keeps this command off another repository's review of the same pull request number.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: FinishTests, the --replace cases, and the rule tests
intro: The review tests run real Git against a bare origin and replace gh with a fake GitHub that records each call and its token. FinishTests covers removing three heads' worktrees, which start comments are deleted and which stay, refusal without --force, a second run, a missing checkout, another model's review, a run from another repository's checkout, and a publish that stopped after it posted. The permission tests check that init adds the new rule beside existing ones.

checks.text: I ran the full suite at f009d62 with Python 3.12: 984 tests passed, with one skip for the Codex rule check, which needs the codex CLI. project check, both claude plugin validate runs, and git diff --check also passed.

files.note: Adds FinishTests, two --replace tests, and a move retry test.

checks.text: Runs finish from a checkout of another repository, with and without --force and --model, and checks that nothing is deleted.
